subject: MAP: TTFT decision matrix & workload profiles (Nova Retail)
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia@novaretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP request: production-like latency test & acceptance gates

Sean / Rachel —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, Nova Retail needs a MAP-backed performance evaluation that mirrors our production traffic before we sign the Dedicated capacity commitment. High-level ask: validate Time-to-First-Token (TTFT), p95 latency, and steady-state throughput at our target concurrencies across the two workload profiles attached (see nova_workloads.xlsx).

Concrete items we want Redwood to scope and own in the MAP:
- Test harness and load-generator config (do you provide or should we run?)
- Workload definitions (short prompts / long prompts, token distributions, prefix caching scenarios)
- Concurrency targets: baseline (8), typical (32), peak (128) — confirm you can reproduce these in Dedicated or a Hosted-equivalent harness
- Success criteria / acceptance gates (p95 TTFT, p50 TTFT, throughput, error rates)
- Test duration per profile and warmup behavior
- Timeline: goal to complete perf validation by Feb 18 to close week of Feb 22

We attached a preliminary workload matrix. Please propose a decision matrix mapping workload -> SLOs and an initial test plan. Also call out any known things that invalidate runs (tokenization variations, dynamic fixtures).

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, Nova Retail
attachments: nova_workloads.xlsx (spreadsheet: profiles, sample prompts)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP request: production-like latency test & acceptance gates

Hi Lydia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the workload spreadsheet. Attached is our recommended MAP benchmarking plan (MAP-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf) and a short decision matrix that maps each Nova profile to SLOs and test parameters. Summary below — please confirm and we'll schedule the runs.

Key decisions and assumptions (short):
- Load harness: Redwood will run the controlled harness in your Dedicated-like environment. We use our continuous-batching-aware driver; we will provide the runner and share configs. If you prefer to run in-house, we can hand off the config.
- Workload profiles (from your sheet):
  * Profile A: interactive short prompts (median tokens: 18, seq len: 64) — target concurrencies: 8 / 32
  * Profile B: document summarization (median tokens: 240, seq len: 512) — target concurrencies: 8 / 32 / 128
  * Cache exercise: repeated prefixes for warm KV cache vs cold-run to measure delta
- SLOs (decision matrix mapping):
  * Acceptance SLO 1 (TTFT): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms for Profile A at concurrency <=32
  * Acceptance SLO 2 (Latency steady-state): p95 < 350ms for Profile B at concurrency <=32; allow up to 500ms at 128 with documented degradation curve
  * Throughput: tokens/sec stable within ±10% during 10-minute steady windows
  * Error rate: successful responses >= 99.5%
- Test duration and sampling: 10-minute warmup, three 20-minute steady-state runs per profile and concurrency, capture full traces + token-level latencies
- Acceptance gates: must meet TTFT & error-rate SLOs for both cold and warm cache runs; if Profile B exceeds 500ms p95 at 128, we'll recommend batching/quant profiles and retest.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue Feb 16: finalize plan + confirm runner access
- Wed Feb 17: baseline runs (Profile A)
- Thu Feb 18: Profile B runs (including 128) & collect artifacts
- Fri Feb 19: Results deck + decision call

Attachments: MAP-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf (plan + decision matrix), drive link to perf workbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcdEg

If that works I'll coordinate internal engineers for the runs and share the runner config.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf (18 pages), runner-config.json (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: TTFT decision matrix & workload profiles (internal notes)

On Mon, Feb 14, 2027 at 11:04 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed timeline:
> - Tue Feb 16: finalize plan + confirm runner access
> - Wed Feb 17: baseline runs (Profile A)
> - Thu Feb 18: Profile B runs (including 128) & collect artifacts
> - Fri Feb 19: Results deck + decision call

Small tweak from perf team after quick review: for the "peak" profile we should run concurrency 64 as an intermediate datapoint before 128 — Nova runs at sustained bursts and we want a smoother degradation curve. Also recommend increasing warmup to 15 minutes for Profile B to stabilize KV cache behavior.

I'll update the plan PDF (v1 -> v1.1) and note the incremental conc 64 run. Marcus, can you allocate one runner on Tue/Wed for the baseline?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Chen <lydia@novaretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: TTFT decision matrix & workload profiles

Sean / team —

Thanks for turning this around quickly. We ran the Redwood-supplied harness in a staging cluster that mirrors our Dedicated instance and attached a CSV with the raw outputs (nova_bench_results_20270216.csv). Highlights:

- Profile A (interactive): p50 TTFT = 62ms, p95 TTFT = 190ms at concurrency 32 (meets SLO)
- Profile B (summarization): p50 TTFT = 210ms, p95 TTFT = 420ms at concurrency 64 (within proposed degradation band)
- Peak 128: p95 TTFT = 610ms and tokens/sec dropped ~18% vs 64 (exceeds the soft limit; we accept this behavior if Redwood documents recommended mitigations)
- Error rate: 99.86% success; a handful of timeouts during the 128-run were tied to transient infra throttles

Decision: Nova will accept the MAP report as sufficient to proceed to contract close provided Redwood includes a short remediation plan for peak-128 behavior (quantization suggestion and effective autoscale knob) and the final artifacts (traces + runner configs). Let's lock for contract signature week of Feb 22.

Thanks again — I'll send a quick note to procurement once I have the remediation text.

Lydia
Lydia Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, Nova Retail
attachments: nova_bench_results_20270216.csv (CSV, 22MB)
